body:
> That's why using the sync point of only calling within `_physics_process()` is necessary afaik.

Just so there's no misunderstanding here, `collider` is the actual scene node that you hit with the query, i.e. `RigidBody3D` in the case where you are using the default physics nodes, and in the case of custom `PhysicsServer3D` objects it's whatever the implementer wants it to be, likely their own scene nodes.

In either case, these are not objects owned by the physics server/thread, nor does it hold any sort of "strong reference" to them, so the objects will never be deleted by it, so there's no sync point to consider here. Any use-after-free here is purely a result of the scene node being freed in some way, which it can't be if it's still referenced by the scene tree, and you can't remove it from the scene tree on anything but the main thread (see [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dfa06cafb4546eac47d863dfa12aec54e4efa586/scene/main/node.cpp#L283-L287)).

Also note that the built-in physics servers already prevent you from retrieving `PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D` on anything but the main thread[^1], and outside of the physics processing in the case of a threaded server, see [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dfa06cafb4546eac47d863dfa12aec54e4efa586/servers/physics_3d/physics_server_3d_wrap_mt.h#L122), [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dfa06cafb4546eac47d863dfa12aec54e4efa586/modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_physics_server_3d.cpp#L194), and [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/dfa06cafb4546eac47d863dfa12aec54e4efa586/modules/jolt_physics/jolt_physics_server_3d.cpp#L234).

So the only data race that's relevant here is unrelated to threading. It's where you perform the query, hold on to the results object, free the object and then access the collider, all of which can happen on the main thread using a non-threaded physics server, from both the physics processing or idle processing[^2].

This shouldn't be any different from the old API that we've had forever now, because scene nodes are not `RefCounted`, so aren't made safe by having their pointer put into a `Dictionary`.

In any case, it's made somewhat better by having `get_collider` call `ObjectDB::get_instance` directly instead. We do still do it "the old way" for extension servers specifically, mostly just to save them the extra `ObjectDB::get_instance` call until they stop populating `collider`, but I'd be fine with dropping this.

[^1]: You can of course bypass all of this by retrieving it on the main thread and then using it on other threads, but that's a separate issue.
[^2]: Doing queries from idle processing is a bad idea for other reasons, but again, separate issue.
